chunks: And I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and His Messenger,
He sent him with the renowned religion, the established standard, the written Book, the radiant light, the shining gleam, and the clear command,
to dispel doubts, present clear proofs, warn through signs, and instill fear through examples.

And the people were in trials wherein the rope of religion was broken, the pillars of certainty were shaken, the course diverged, the matter became scattered, the exit was narrow, and the source was darkened,
so guidance was obscure, and blindness prevailed.
ai.seo_question: What are the attributes of the religion and light sent with Prophet Muhammad according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi frames this testimony not merely as a declaration of faith but as a theological argument for the Prophet's role as the definitive resolver of ambiguity (Izāhat al-shubuhāt) amidst the fragmentation of the pre-Islamic era. The text emphasizes the completeness of the divine message (Kitab MASTUR) as a remedy for the 'narrow exit' (Dāq al-makhraj) and spiritual blindness that characterized the Age of Ignorance, a theme central to Shia exegetical understanding of the Prophet's mission. This context highlights the transition from chaotic ignorance to structured certainty through the 'clear signs' (Bayyināt) and 'warnings' (Ayāt) provided by the Prophet.

en.sayed-ali-raza: I also stand witness that Muḥammad (S) is His. slave and His Prophet.
Allāh sent him with the illustrious religion, effective emblem, written Book, [1] effulgent light, sparkling gleam and decisive injunction
in order to dispel doubts, present clear proofs, administer warning through signs and to warn of punishments.

At that time people had fallen in vices whereby the rope of religion had been broken, the pillars of belief had been shaken, principles had been sacrileged, system had become topsy-turvy, openings were narrow, passage was dark,
guidance was unknown and darkness prevailed.
